title: U.S. House · Illinois's 5th District
area: Chicago's North Side lakefront and northern Cook County suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Mike Quigley (D) defeated Matthew Conroy, Ellen Corley, and Anthony Michael Tamez in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Tom Hanson defeated Barry Wicker and Kimball Ladien in the Republican primary.

summary.text: Quigley has represented Illinois' 5th Congressional District since a 2009 special election. A lawyer and law professor, he served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners from 1998 to 2009 before entering Congress. He sits on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and the Appropriations Committee, and is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1958; according to his official biography, he grew up in Carol Stream, Illinois, and worked his way through college.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Roosevelt University (1981), a master's degree in public policy from the University of Chicago (1985), and a law degree from Loyola University School of Law (1989).
Worked as a lawyer and as a law professor before entering elected office.
Served on the Cook County Board of Commissioners for District 10 from 1998 to 2009, where, according to his official biography, he worked to increase transparency on the board.
Was elected to Congress to represent Illinois' 5th District on April 7, 2009, succeeding Rahm Emanuel.

Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and on the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development; he is also co-chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and Vice-Chair of the LGBT Equality Caucus, per his official biography.

Founded the bipartisan Congressional Transparency Caucus. His Congressional Budget Justification Act was signed into law in 2021, and his ACT for ALS, introduced in 2020, was signed into law in December 2021, according to his official biography.
Teaches a course on intelligence and national security at the University of Chicago and lives in Chicago with his wife, Barb, according to his official biography.

priorities.text: Our economy was significantly impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. Millions of Americans lost jobs, businesses closed, and nearly every industry was at a standstill. I worked hard since 2020 to ensure Chicago businesses could get back on their feet.
Health care is an essential right, and a healthy America is a more productive, safer, and better place to call home.

We live in a time of unprecedented threat to our environment. From pollution to habitat degradation to the global crisis of man-made climate change, the evidence all around us is clear that we must act to protect our planet and everything living on it.

positions.summary: Says he has sponsored and cosponsored gun violence prevention legislation, including universal background checks and an assault weapons ban.
positions.quote: I have supported measures including requiring mandatory background checks on 100 percent of gun sales; limiting the sale of assault weapons and high-capacity magazines; improving the National Instant Background Check System to keep weapons out of the hands of criminals and the mentally ill; implementing buyback programs; and requiring tougher penalties for criminals caught trafficking guns across state lines.

positions.summary: Says he will always stand up for reproductive rights and describes abortion care as health care after the overturning of Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Put simply, abortion care is health care.

positions.summary: Says he voted for the Affordable Care Act and continues to fight to protect coverage for preexisting conditions, and supported the Inflation Reduction Act's Medicare drug-price negotiation.
positions.quote: I was proud that one of my earliest votes in Congress was for the Affordable Care Act (ACA) because it ensures that millions of Americans have access to affordable, quality health care.

positions.summary: Serves as Co-Chair of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition and says Congress must act on man-made climate change and move toward a low-carbon economy.
positions.quote: I serve as Co-Chair of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC), a group of more than 87 members of the House of Representatives committed to combating climate change and ensuring a robust, resilient, low-carbon economy for generations to come.

positions.summary: In a January 2026 press release he called for dismantling ICE in its current form and rebuilding the agency.
positions.quote: We must dismantle Trump’s ICE from the top down

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Subcommittees on Legislative Branch and on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs) in the 119th Congress.
Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (Subcommittees on Defense Intelligence and Overhead Architecture, and Open Source Intelligence) in the 119th Congress.
Chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Hanson is a Chicago-born small business owner who works in commercial real estate and has run for this seat in several earlier cycles. He won the March 2026 Republican primary. His campaign website describes him as a "Liberal Republican – fiscally conservative/socially liberal."

background.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, and lives in Illinois.
According to his campaign website, he began his career selling advertising for the Chicago Tribune and later U.S. News & World Report, and now works selling and leasing commercial real estate.
Describes himself as owning a small business; Ballotpedia lists his profession as business owner.
Was the Republican nominee for this seat in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024 and lost each general election to Mike Quigley; he won the Republican primary in each of those years.
Won the Republican primary on March 17, 2026, and is on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot.

priorities.text: Names reducing federal spending and the deficit as an economic priority.
Names prosecuting violent criminals and supporting law enforcement as a crime priority.
priorities.quote: I believe in prosecuting and keeping violent criminals in jail as long as legally possible so that they cannot victimize more innocent people.

priorities.text: Says he believes in lawful immigration and opposes illegal immigration.
priorities.quote: I believe in robust, lawful immigration.

positions.quote: I am pro-life and believe that every person deserves the opportunity to pursue life, liberty and happiness.

statements.quote: I.C.E. will only work in the states that demand their services; This change will reduce unwanted federal services and federal expenditures, leaving it up to each state to make that decision.
Replace individual income taxes with corporations making up the difference for federal taxes. Plus implementing sensible tariffs and a Fair Tax, for generating revenue for our government.
Demand residential landlords maintain their rental properties and cooperate with their tenants.
